events.text: README status: boots, intro video with sound, menus at 30 fps, saves work, loads into the world — scene still dark, 0.5–1.8 s per frame
README status: starts in ~4 s, menus at a steady 30 fps, reaches settings — gameplay not reached, minimap mesh pipelines refused
Pipeline build stuck near 21k of 26,503 — one NVIDIA compute shader ran 95+ min, 2 out-of-memory errors
Runtime rebuilt 496/496 · tests 274/276 passing
Reaches main loop at a steady 60 fps — frames still black; main thread waits on a frame-graph task
Compute pipelines missing from the cache now compile in the background — boot no longer stalls on 40–140 s driver compiles
Fixed a first-frame deadlock that tripped the game's hang watchdog — down to one window
GPU address arena raised from 256 MiB to 4 GiB — job system drains (528 → 16 pending) and the null-pointer crash is gone
2,717 runtime FSPX/FidelityFX programs dumped and decoded (28 s instead of hours); 1,799 translated to SPIR-V
Console RegisterPagePool implemented — the 6 GiB GPU pool now registers; bindless texture tables enlarged
BCPack decoder wired into DirectStorage; XMA audio decoding enabled — matches ffmpeg on all 1,818 streams
Now: game runs stable at 30 fps for 3+ minutes. Blocker: textures in the game's own GPU memory pool aren't visible to the GPU yet, so everything samples black — detile + upload in progress
Title textures: textures the game streams into its own memory are now detiled and uploaded to the GPU — 346 textures, 0 failures
Console CopyPageMappingsBatchX implemented: 1,521 pages of the 6 GiB pool now mapped into the GPU tiled heap — how GTA VI streams textures
Presentation verified end to end: a forced magenta clear shows on screen, so the black comes from the game's own frame content
Black splash draw: depth, culling, viewport and scissor ruled out — full 3840×2160 viewport, one render target, but no pixels written yet
Blocker now: the game's buffers in its own memory aren't GPU-visible yet (textures are), so the splash draw likely reads zeros — tracing it
Startup crash fixed (hit ~half of runs at ~12 s): the 6 GiB GPU pool is now mapped as page runs instead of 99,776 separate views — closed a race in the texture streamer
Buffer shadows: the game's 182 MB constant ring and placed buffers now reach the GPU — constant, root and vertex data copied every frame (~74 KB/frame)
Black screen explained: for the first time the GPU reads the game's real vertex data — it's drawing its own full-screen black fade triangle, so black is correct for this state
Next: find what the game waits for on the fade frame (923 runtime shader programs still untranslated, mesh amplification shaders, unshadowed buffers). Also open: one crash after ~212 s
World renders for the first time with an opt-in switch (XCL_PSO_WAIT_MS): sky, clouds and terrain, under 1 fps, not playable yet (PR #891 merged)
Shader translator: wave32 VCC_HI now handled as an ordinary register — runtime shader programs translating jumped from 1,799 to 2,516 of 2,717
Texture sizes now match the console's tiled layout — fixed a 1×1 cube texture overrunning its heap block by 20 KiB; the game's heap asserts are gone
sRGB/UNORM views of the same console texture now work — no more rejected render-target views
Vertex data in the game's own memory now reaches the GPU via on-demand copies — zero command lists rejected
Crash reports now capture CPU registers and the memory each object points to
Blocker now: at ~65 s something overwrites an object's vtable with float data (1.0, 1.0) — hunting the bad write. After that: direct GPU access to game memory (VK_EXT_external_memory_host)
~65 s crash FIXED: the game maps textures to fill them on the CPU; the PC layer refused and left a stale pointer, so 4 KiB of texels landed on the game's heap. Map now returns the texture's CPU copy
Found it with a new write-watch diagnostic that traps writes into a heap window and logs the instruction doing the write
Boot now runs the full 150 s test at a steady 30 fps (2,884 frames), no crash, every GPU command list submitted
Next: thread stacks at 90 s and 140 s to see what the game waits for on the black loading fade
Mystery solved: the black fade was the game waiting for a button press on the "press start" screen we couldn't see (boot stage 4)
GameInput shim built (SDL3 3.4.20) and bound to the game's ordinal import — it was silently using Windows' own GameInput
🔊 FIRST AUDIO: a scripted A-press every 3 s gets past "press start" — the game moves on to boot state 13, runs 260 s with no crash, and its audio plays
Black screen cause: ~19,000 draws land in off-screen targets, but the final image goes to the 4K screen via compute — and every compute dispatch is skipped while NVIDIA compiles them
NVIDIA takes 60–190 s per translated compute shader (3–4 MB SPIR-V modules, 24 compiling at once). Next: shrink the translator output or precompile them into the driver cache
FIRST RENDERED FRAME: the game's first-boot settings menu now draws (purple background, "Navigation experience: Minimap", CONTINUE (A)) with 100% of pixels drawn, steady 30 fps

Black-screen root cause: Xbox shaders read their arguments starting at register s8 (s0-s7 belong to the system). Leonida packed them from s0, so every menu shader read zeros and drew nothing. Fixed, and constant buffers now use the console's 16-byte stride
New frame-capture tool saves every GPU command and every image of a frame to disk. It pinned down the bug in four runs
Shader compiles are now cached across runs, with the shaders a frame needs compiled first. On the second run every compute dispatch runs from the first second
2,642 of 2,717 run-time compute shaders now translate (+126)
Keyboard control works: Enter = A, arrows = d-pad, Backspace = B, Esc = Menu
Next: find the console's own compose-to-screen step (the menu reaches the window through a stand-in for now), then the main menu and the intro movie
Menus now render fullscreen on PC, with the first frames captured. Run s169 is testing the next two fixes
Startup video was black: the game's placed buffer views reached the GPU as empty descriptors. They now point at real copies of game memory
Missing letters: a CPU copy overwrote the GPU-uploaded font pages every frame. Pages are now uploaded only when the CPU actually wrote them
Next: the crash after "Finish setup?" (82 shaders still untranslated + one missing pipeline)
Startup videos now play on PC: the game's placed buffer views get real GPU copies of game memory
"Finish setup?" crash fixed: Map on buffers the game placed in its own memory now returns that memory, as on the console. The run goes past setup into world streaming
One window: a black Leonida window opens at launch and the game's white window stays hidden
Picture alignment fix in testing: the swap chain resizes with the window, and the window is DPI-aware
Next blocker: a crash in CopyPageMappingsBatchX (wrong batch layout) when the world starts streaming. Menus run at 10-15 fps for now
Default build still stops in world loading: the game's GPU watchdog fires while giant compute shaders (up to 30 MB) build; testers on issue #505 are splitting them up
Reaches the world load: in-world audio heard. Blocker: a GPU crash in one of three compute shaders, caught with NVIDIA checkpoints
Fixed: title memory below 1 TiB (40-bit ray-tracing address error), console texture sizes (no more over-reads), background texture conversion, failed loading reads
VRAM leak fixed: dead texture copies freed and duplicates shared, 11.7 → 5.8 GB. New texture-quality setting for 8 GB GPUs
30 fps menus and intro videos · first frame at ~13 s
Next: find which of three compute shaders (fspx/runtime 425, 356, 678) kills the GPU, then fix its translation

Shader-compile stall in world load fixed: a shader the game needs right now compiles at once on the game's own thread (0.4 s instead of a 30 s queue wait that tripped the freeze watchdog). World load gets further: 1,612 frames vs 1,469
All 5,458 compute shaders now pre-compile in the background into a cache for later starts
Next blocker: a game setting in memory gets overwritten during world load. A write-trap run is in progress to find the writer
Texture fix in progress: about 8% of compressed BC7/BC6H texture blocks came out blank. The decoder is getting calibrated history tables
Textures: the BC7/BC6H decoder now uses history tables calibrated from the player's own files. Blank chunks 185 → 52 per 2,048 (70% fewer)
GPU data safety: the per-frame CPU → GPU copy now sends only the 256-byte chunks the CPU actually changed (a third of what it looked at), so data the GPU wrote is no longer overwritten
Crash pinned down: GPU device losses now always name the exact shader. The world-load hang is a translator bug in FidelityFX shader runtime_2390 (wave64 emulation on NVIDIA), now being fixed
